latestRelease.title: v0.21.8
latestRelease.notes:
## v0.21.8 - 2026-07-29

### Changed

- Changeset diffs are now computed from filesystem metadata instead of full-content comparison, significantly speeding up diff computation for large directories. by @marcosnils in
  https://github.com/dagger/dagger/pull/13615

### Fixed

- Dockerfile build layer caching so unrelated build-context changes no longer bust the cache: `COPY`-ed directories now get a content-based cache identity, re-keying downstream steps only when copied content
  actually changes. by @marcosnils in https://github.com/dagger/dagger/pull/13765
- The `--x-release` CLI re-exec so `_EXPERIMENTAL_DAGGER_RUNNER_HOST` is preserved (with a warning) instead of being stripped, and clarified its startup message to avoid implying it runs from any build. by
  @tiborvass in https://github.com/dagger/dagger/pull/13752
- Silent SDK sessions no longer retain frontend telemetry in memory while Cloud and OTLP export remain enabled. `DAGGER_SILENT` is now honored as the equivalent of `--silent`. by @sipsma in
  https://github.com/dagger/dagger/pull/13762

### What to do next?

- Read the [documentation](https://docs.dagger.io)
- Join our [Discord server](https://discord.gg/dagger-io)
- Follow us on [Twitter](https://twitter.com/dagger_io)

signals.title: Crash on stale SSH_AUTH_SOCK during module codegen
signals.text: Originally reported in https://github.com/dagger/dagger/discussions/12660 When `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` points to a stale or non-existent socket, module operations crash with a cryptic EOF error even when SSH features aren't being used. Fix: #12849

signals.title: Native Dagger Engine Scoping to prevent collisions
signals.text: ### What are you trying to do? As I start to daggerize more of my projects, if I run dagger in two different directories at the same time, they collide. AI had me do the following - and it works - but it would be so much better if Dagger did this more easily. I am worried about running parallel builds on the same Jenkins agent as well. ``` #!/usr/bin/env bash # # Callers are expected to set `_EXPERIMENTAL_DAGGER_RUNNER_HOST= # docker-container://$DAGGER_ENGINE` for their OWN invocation immediately # after this succeeds -- never globally in `[env]`. `docker-container://`, # unlike dagger's default scheme, never auto-creates a container, so a # process that inherits it without having run this script first hangs # indefinitely instead of failing fast (confirmed live, 2026-08-12: every # `dagger_cli.dagger_call` in a real `mat` run hung on a branch engine that # had never been created). Running this first is what makes setting that # variable safe. # # Shared by `[tasks.dagger]` and `[tasks.run-dart]` rather than inlined in # both: a DART's `dagger` calls come from `dagger_cli.py`'s own # `subprocess.run(["dagger", ...])`, which never goes through mise's # `dagger` shell alias (execve doesn't expand aliases), so the two entry # points genuinely both need this and must not drift apart. set -euo pipefail engine="${DAGGER_ENGINE:?DAGGER_ENGINE must be set (see mise.toml [env])}" branch="${BRANCH:?BRANCH must be set (see mise.toml [env])}" project="${PROJECT_NAME:?PROJECT_NAME must be set (see mise.toml [env])}" if docker ps -q -f "name=^/${engine}$" | grep -q .; then # Already running -- the socket is necessarily up, nothing to wait for. exit 0 fi # `docker start` first: a stopped container still holds this branch's build # cache, so recreating it would silently throw that away. if docker start "$engine" 2>/dev/null; then # Restarting an existing engine only needs its socket re-bound. attempts=30 # 6s else # Redirect docker.io through the internal Artifactory mirror. Without it, # a COLD engine pulls every module's SDK base image (e.g. # `docker.io/library/python:3.14-slim`) anonymously and this shared # devstack's egress IP trips Docker Hub's rate limit: confirmed live # 2026-08-16, a `mat` run died at `stage=create` in 16s with # "429 Too Many Requests / You have reached your unauthenticated pull # rate limit" while merely loading `dart-catalog`. Latent until now only # because the previously long-lived shared engine had a warm cache -- # branch-scoped engines are created far more often, so an unmirrored # cold start is now the common case, not a rare one. # # Mounted only when the file exists, so a caller that sets nothing still # gets a working (if unmirrored) engine rather than a hard failure on a # missing path. TOML at that exact path because the engine image's own # entrypoint always runs `dagger-engine --config /etc/dagger/engine.toml`. # Same approach as ngp-ui's mise.toml, which hit this first. engine_config_mount=() if [ -n "${DAGGER_ENGINE_CONFIG:-}" ] && [ -f "${DAGGER_ENGINE_CONFIG}" ]; then engine_config_mount=(-v "${DAGGER_ENGINE_CONFIG}:/etc/dagger/engine.toml") fi # Cache volume scoped by project AND branch, mirroring DAGGER_ENGINE's own # naming: a named Docker volume is global to the host, not per-container, # so branch alone let two repos on this box collide whenever both built a # same-named branch (`integration`). Their engine containers were already # separate; the volume was not. ngp-ui fixed this exact collision first. docker run -d --name "$engine" --privileged \ -v "dagger-cache-${project}-${branch}:/var/lib/dagger" \ "${engine_config_mount[@]}" \ "registry.dagger.io/engine:$(dagger version | cut -d' ' -f2)" >/dev/null # A first-run engine may still be pulling its image, so 6s (what a # restart needs) would fail a genuinely-healthy cold start. Still # bounded -- the point of the original 30x0.2s loop was to fail fast # with a real cause instead of hanging forever on a socket that will # never appear, and 2min preserves that while being honest about how # long a cold start actually takes. attempts=600 # 2min fi for _ in $(seq 1 "$attempts"); do if docker exec "$engine" test -S /var/run/dagger/engine.sock 2>/dev/null; then exit 0 fi sleep 0.2 done echo "ERROR: $engine never became ready (no engine.sock after $((attempts / 5))s)" >&2 exit 1 ``` ### Why is this important to you? _No response_ ### How are you currently working around this? _No response_
